criteria_source: The fixture only. RETENTION.md defines a soft-delete window in which deleting an account sets deleted_at and removes nothing, hides the account from every product surface, refuses login and revokes sessions, stops email and expires export links, for 30 days, during which support can restore the account and its data is complete and unchanged. It defines a hard purge, a nightly job that takes accounts whose deletion is more than 30 days old, deletes their rows from 14 tables, has their stored objects deleted within 24 hours, and writes a tombstone without personal data to an audit ledger, after which the account cannot be restored, with a verification job checking no rows remain. It states that backups are not purged: nightly database snapshots are kept for 35 days and never rewritten, so a purged account still exists in backups for up to 35 days after its purge, up to 65 days after the deletion request; the date given to a user for an erasure request is the backup expiry, and a backup restore replays the purge ledger before taking traffic. None of it comes from rules/laconic.md.
trap:
Passes when the answer explains both steps from RETENTION.md and carries the backup caveat. The soft-delete window: deleting an account only marks it deleted and hides it (login refused, invisible in the product, email stopped), keeping its data intact for 30 days so support can restore it. The hard purge: after the 30 days a nightly job permanently deletes the account's data from the database and its stored files, records an audit tombstone, and verifies the deletion; after that the account cannot be restored. The caveat: backups are not purged, so a purged account survives in database snapshots for up to 35 more days (up to about 65 days after the request), which is why the erasure date given to a user is the backup expiry and why a restore from backup has to replay the purge ledger. Fails when the soft-delete window is described as deleting data, when the purge is described as reversible, or when the backup caveat is missing or inverted, such as stating that a purged account is gone everywhere at the purge.

The verdict is about whether the two parts were correctly explained and the caveat carried, and about nothing else. Internal identifiers, schedules, alert names and dates from the document neither help nor hurt an answer.

A response that asks which document or which stages are meant, rather than reading RETENTION.md, is NOT EXERCISED.
